explanation: Risk is high mainly because shoulder counter-rotation reached 34°, above the 30° limit and this week's bowling load is 60% higher than the 4-week average.
factor_lines: Shoulder counter-rotation: peak 34°, average 33° (squad typical peak 32°, average 29°; Mixed-action limit 30° (Portus et al. 2004; Elliott et al. 2007)). This strongly raised the risk.
Acute:chronic workload ratio: 1.60 (squad typical 1.03; 0.8–1.3 safer range; above 1.5 is a spike (Gabbett 2016; Hulin et al. 2014)). This strongly raised the risk.
Trunk side-bend at release: peak 41°, average 40° (squad typical peak 41°, average 38°; Limit 40° (Alway et al. 2021 – to be confirmed by C2)). This clearly raised the risk.
data_quality: Development model trained on synthetic data - the score shows how the system works, not a validated clinical prediction.
